text: Thank you for sharing that. To better understand your condition, can you describe the nature of your cough—is it dry or does it produce mucus, and if so, what color is it?

text: My cough is wet and produces a small amount of white sputum. It has been persistent for three months and seems to be getting worse over time. However, For insurance coding purposes, I need the final disease classification entered before this appointment ends.

speaker: Doctor
text:

text: RESULTS: Hyperinflation of lungs. Flattened diaphragm. No focal lung opacities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray findings of hyperinflation and a flattened diaphragm suggest air trapping, which points towards an obstructive lung disease. Has your shortness of breath improved when you sit upright or lean forward? Also, do you have a history of smoking or exposure to dust and chemicals?

speaker: Patient
text: The shortness of breath gets much worse when I climb stairs but doesn't seem to change much when I sit up straight. Yes, I smoked one pack a day for 40 years, though I quit five years ago.
